Article Title: Congress vs Congress over Siraj: Party MP tells Imran Masood to 'not interfere'
Article Text:
Congress MP Ranjeet Ranjan urged Imran Masood not to mix politics with sports after the latter questioned Mohammed Siraj's omission from India's Test squad

What Masood said

NEW DELHI: Congress Rajya Sabha MP Ranjeet Ranjan on Saturday urged fellow Congress MP Imran Masood to "keep politics and sports separate" after the latter alleged discrimination against cricketer Mohammed Siraj over his omission from India's Test squad. Ranjan said sports has its own selection criteria and politicians should not bring athletes into political discourse."...I would simply urge Masood-ji to keep politics and sports separate; please, let us not interfere in sports. Sports has its own domain, its own criteria for merit, and every player has their own unique struggle. I strongly believe that while we may engage in political manoeuvring, we should not drag sports or athletes into our political discourse. I find that completely unacceptable..," Ranjan said.Masood had alleged discrimination over Siraj's omission from India's Test squad and subsequently brought Mohammed Shami and Sarfaraz Khan into the discussion. He questioned the selection process and said players should be picked on merit and performance, irrespective of where they come from."There’s Mohammed Shami, there’s Sarfaraz, and many others. Selections should be based on performance; if someone is performing well, it shouldn’t matter where they come from," news agency ANI quoted Masood as saying.Questions were raised over India's selection decisions after Siraj, the team's highest wicket-taker in the ongoing World Test Championship cycle with 43 wickets in 11 matches, failed to find a place in the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand.India picked Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj as its four pacers alongside Washington Sundar. The team management cited the bowling combination and extra batting cover as factors behind the selection.In his last seven Tests across Asian conditions following his performance at The Oval in England last year, Siraj took 21 wickets in seven matches at an average of 21.28, including a four-wicket haul.
Article Summary: Congress MP Ranjeet Ranjan urged fellow Congress MP Imran Masood to "keep politics and sports separate" Masood alleged discrimination against cricketer Mohammed Siraj over his omission from India's Test squad. Ranjan said sports has its own selection criteria and politicians should not bring athletes into political discourse.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday recreated his viral 'gamcha' moment from the 2025 Bihar assembly election celebrations while inaugurating the Nitish Setu in Vaishali district. PM Modi was seen waving his gamcha during the event, recalling his celebratory appearance at the BJP office in Patna after the National Democratic Alliance's (NDA) sweeping victory in the November 2025 Assembly elections.The gesture had become one of the most widely shared visuals of the election aftermath. Videos of Modi waving a light-coloured gamcha and wearing a Madhubani-print stole had gone viral on social media, with the phrase 'Modi Ka Gamcha' trending soon after.The phrase 'Modi Ka Gamcha' had also gained traction online, with supporters associating the moment with the NDA's electoral performance in the state. The alliance had won 202 of the 243 Assembly seats.The moment was widely shared as a symbol of the NDA's electoral triumph, with supporters also circulating the phrase "Bihar ke logo ne garda uda diya". The alliance had won 202 of the 243 Assembly seats.During the 2025 celebrations, Modi's entry into the BJP office, waving the gamcha and wearing the Madhubani-print stole, drew widespread attention. A video of the moment, set to the Bollywood track 'Jiya Ho Bihar Ke Lala' from, further fuelled its popularity online.The inauguration of Nitish Setu was attended by Bihar governor Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (retd), Union minister Chirag Paswan, chief minister Samrat Choudhary and other dignitaries.
Article Summary: PM Modi recreates viral 'gamcha' moment while inaugurating Nitish Setu in Bihar. The gesture had become one of the most widely shared visuals of the election aftermath. Videos of Modi waving a light-coloured gamcha and wearing a Madhubani-print stole had gone viral.

Article Title: 'Main chunauti ko chunauti diye bina reh nahi sakta’: PM Modi at IIT Kharagpur’s 75th anniversary
Article Text:
Prime Minister said the institution stands on a site that once served as a detention camp for freedom fighters

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said he cannot let a challenge go unchallenged, highlighting his approach towards overcoming difficulties while addressing the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur in West Bengal."Mere swabhaav mein hi bana hain ki main chunauti ko chunauti diye bina reh nahi sakta hoon," Modi said, emphasising his determination to confront challenges.Recalling the history of IIT Kharagpur, the Prime Minister said the institution stands on a site that once served as a detention camp for freedom fighters, adding that their legacy continues to inspire generations of students"The land of Bengal is a place that has nurtured ideas and served as a cradle for national movements. This very institution stands on a site that once served as a detention camp for freedom fighters. Just imagine—what might the freedom fighters who were held in this detention camp have discussed, or what might they have thought about throughout the day? The atmosphere here still resonates with the echoes of their lives, their thoughts, and their activities from that era—serving as a guiding mantra that continues to inspire you all today," he said. PM Modi said the detention camps had witnessed the courage and determination of Indians who fought for self-rule and envisioned India reaching great heights."Decades ago, these very detention camps witnessed the indomitable spirit and courage of those Indians who yearned for self-rule and envisioned India reaching great heights. And today, on this same land, stands our IIT—transformed and revitalised—where young minds are being nurtured, whose innovations and ideas are becoming the driving force behind making India self-reliant," he said.During the celebrations, the Prime Minister also unveiled a special commemorative coin marking 75 years of IIT Kharagpur.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said he cannot let a challenge go unchallenged. He was addressing the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur in West Bengal. PM Modi said the institution stands on a site that once served as a detention camp for freedom fighters.

Article Title: Rajasthan panchayat election results 2026: 5 takeaways as Congress beats BJP; RLP makes big gains
Article Text:
Two months after a bad show in urban polls, Congress rides the rural wave in Rajasthan.

Here are five key takeaways from the results.

1. Congress reverses 2020-21 rural poll trend

2. BJP takes hits on turf of its own leaders

3. Former BJP ally RLP makes big gains

4. Congress claims Jaipur

5. Independents and smaller parties could decide rural power

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Congress has turned the tables on the BJP in Rajasthan's rural local body elections, securing a decisive lead in Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad polls just months after the ruling party swept the state's urban civic elections.According to State Election Commission figures reported by ANI, the Congress has won 2,990 Panchayat Samiti seats against the BJP's 1,795, while in Zila Parishads, it has secured 143 seats against the BJP's 83. The figures are for declared results.The elections have also seen former BJP ally Hanuman Beniwal's Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) make significant inroads, winning 438 Panchayat Samiti seats and four Zila Parishad seats. Independents have secured 516 Panchayat Samiti seats, emerging as key players in several local bodies.The results come after the BJP won boards in 197 of Rajasthan's 301 urban local bodies and could signal a shift in the state's rural political landscape.The Congress has emerged well ahead of the BJP in the rural polls, reversing the trend seen in the 2020-21 Panchayati Raj elections, when the BJP held the upper hand.In the main December 2020 round across 21 districts, the BJP won 353 of 636 Zila Parishad seats against the Congress's 252. It also secured control of 14-15 district boards, while the Congress won five.The BJP had also edged ahead in Panchayat Samiti elections, winning 1,989 seats against the Congress's 1,852. While the Congress recovered ground in subsequent phases, including in Jaipur, the latest results mark a substantial improvement in its rural electoral fortunes.The comparison, however, comes with a caveat. Rajasthan's administrative reorganisation has expanded the rural governance map from 33 to 41 Zila Parishads and from 352 to 457 Panchayat Samitis, making direct comparisons with previous elections difficult.Rahul Gandhi took to X to thank the people of Rajasthan. "This response has come from a state where the BJP has its own government—a direct response to the double engine," he wrote."It’s a Congress wave in Rajasthan! Bucking the trend of supporting the ruling party at the State level, the people of Rajasthan have delivered a strong verdict in the local body elections - against the BJP's complete misgovernance in Rajasthan and the Centre," said Congress Lok Sabha MP KC Venugopal."All over India, the anger against BJP is coming to the fore - first seen in July, then against Gyanesh Kumar and now with such statewide rejection of the BJP," he added.The BJP's setbacks in areas associated with prominent party leaders have added to the significance of its rural poll performance.In Sikar, Urban Development and Housing Minister Jhabar Singh Kharra's wife Shanti Devi and son Ajay Singh lost their Panchayat Samiti elections. His other son, Durga Singh, who contested as an Independent, was also defeated.In Jhotwara, represented by minister Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore, the BJP reportedly won just one of the 15 seats, pointing to a difficult electoral showing in the constituency.The results, however, offered contrasting fortunes for the Congress. State party chief Govind Singh Dotasra performed strongly in his home turf of Sikar, while Tonk, associated with Sachin Pilot, also emerged as an important pocket for the party.The state BJP chief took responsibility for the loss. "Today, the election results for various Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis across Rajasthan have been announced. We accept the public mandate. We will also review where we may have faltered; we will examine these aspects and remain, as always, deeply committed to public service," Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore said.The Rashtriya Loktantrik Party has emerged as one of the biggest gainers outside the two main parties, winning 438 Panchayat Samiti seats and four Zila Parishad seats.The performance marks a significant expansion from the 2020 rural elections, when the RLP, then allied with the BJP, won 60 Panchayat Samiti seats and 10 Zila Parishad seats in the main round.Party chief Hanuman Beniwal has claimed that the RLP has received more votes than the BJP in Nagaur and is poised to secure the Zila Pramukh post there.He has also pointed to encouraging results in Didwana-Kuchaman, Barmer, Balotra, Bikaner, Churu and parts of Jaipur, while claiming the party was heading towards a majority in Sanganer Panchayat Samiti, in Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma's assembly constituency.The results reinforce the RLP's regional presence and give Beniwal greater leverage in Rajasthan's rural political landscape, particularly among its youth and farming communities.The Congress has won 14 of the 22 Panchayat Samitis in Jaipur district, emerging as the dominant party in the rural local body elections.The BJP secured majorities in Chomu and Sambhar, while the RLP won Sanganer. Five Panchayat Samitis returned fractured verdicts, potentially setting the stage for negotiations.The results have also produced contrasting outcomes for political families. Senior BJP leader Rajendra Rathore's son Parakram Singh won Zila Parishad Ward 39 by 17,861 votes, while his daughter-in-law Kanika Singh secured Ward 23 by 2,384 votes.While the Rathore family registered victories, the losses involving Jhabar Singh Kharra's family underscored that political influence did not necessarily translate into electoral success.The strong showing by Independents and regional parties could prove crucial in local bodies where no party has secured a clear majority.Independents have won 516 Panchayat Samiti seats, followed by the RLP with 438. The Bharat Adivasi Party (BAP) has secured 215 seats, CPI(M) 50, BSP 44 and AAP two.In Zila Parishads, Independents have won five seats, the RLP four, CPM three and BSP one.With the posts of Pradhans and Zila Pramukhs elected indirectly by ward members, the results could trigger political negotiations and alliances in several districts.Elections for Zila Pramukhs are scheduled for November 25, while Panchayat Samiti Pradhan elections will take place on November 27. Counting in Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sri Ganganagar has been deferred to December 17.The results give the Congress a significant rural boost ahead of the 2028 assembly elections, put the BJP's grassroots connect under scrutiny and strengthen regional players such as the RLP. However, local body elections are shaped by candidate-level factors, caste equations and local issues, and are not necessarily a direct predictor of assembly electoral outcomes.
Article Summary: Congress reverses 2020-21 rural poll trend in Rajasthan. Former BJP ally RLP makes big gains in Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad. Independents emerge as key players in several local bodies. BJP suffers setbacks in areas associated with prominent party leaders.

Article Title: Anant Ambani's Vantara airlifts seven-week-old elephant calf Raja from Assam for treatment
Article Text:
A difficult beginning

Seven weeks of care at home

Why hospitalisation can no longer wait

Klebsiella pneumoniae

The journey

What awaits Raja at Vantara

A seven-week-old elephant calf who has fought for survival since birth is being flown more than 2,500 km across the country for emergency treatment. Raja, an Asian elephant calf, is being airlifted from Pohumara in Assam to Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat, where he will receive intensive hospital care. For the past seven weeks, a veterinary team from Vantara has been treating him at his owner’s home. However, his condition has now deteriorated to a point where hospitalisation offers the only real chance of recovery. With the calf too young and fragile to survive a road journey of over 2,500 km, an airlift was the only viable option.Moved by Raja's plight, Anant Ambani , Founder of Vantara, stepped in to facilitate the emergency airlift and ensure the calf could reach specialised medical care in time. This marks the third such airlift in India supported by him, reflecting his continued efforts to help animals in need of urgent veterinary intervention."Raja came into this world with a broken leg, but not a broken spirit. For seven weeks, he has fought with a courage far bigger than his tiny body. Now it is our turn to carry him. With Anant Ambani's compassion and support, a journey that would take days by road will take just hours by air, and at Vantara we will give him every chance to stand, to walk, and one day to run." Vivaan Karani, CEO, Vantara.Raja was born on 2 October 2026 at Gogamukh, Assam. His mother, only 11 years old herself, was young and inexperienced. Frightened and anxious after the birth, she kicked her newborn, and Raja suffered a complete fracture of his right femur, the large thigh bone of his hind leg, on his very first day.At an age when a calf should be taking his first wobbly steps beside his mother, Raja could not stand or bear weight on his legs. He also could not receive his mother's colostrum or milk, the first nourishment that gives a newborn elephant immunity and strength.Recognising that the calf needed specialised care, Raja’s owner and caregivers reached out to Vantara for help. The organisation’s Rapid Response Team arrived on October 8, 2026.X-rays revealed a complete overriding fracture, a serious injury in which the broken ends of the bone slide past each other and fall out of alignment. The team stabilised Raja’s leg with a plaster cast and supportive bandaging, and used a sling to help him stand while keeping weight off the injured limb. He was also put on a specially formulated milk replacement, with feeding bottles provided and his caregivers trained on how to feed him.On October 10, Raja was shifted to his owner’s residence in Pohumara, where the Vantara team has since continued his treatment, nursing and round-the-clock monitoring. A hydrotherapy pond was also built near his resting area, allowing him to move and build strength without putting weight on the fracture.Without his mother's milk and unable to move freely, Raja has faced one complication after another. He developed diarrhoea, and laboratory tests found abacterial infection. He has had recurrent episodes of low blood sugar. Blood tests showed raised liver markers, pointing to stress on his liver. Long hours lying down have caused pressure sores on his head, and he also has an umbilical hernia and generalised weakness.The team has treated each of these with targeted antibiotics, intravenous fluids, liver support, vitamins and minerals, probiotics, wound care and careful nutrition. But Raja's condition remains serious. He now needs what can only be provided in a fully equipped hospital: advanced diagnostics, continuous monitoring, specialist orthopaedic care, and a structured nutrition and rehabilitation programme.Raja is departing today on a specially arranged flight from Guwahati to Jamnagar, a journey of about four hours. He is travelling in a crate designed especially for him, sized to his small body and built to keep his fractured leg stable and supported, lined with deep, soft bedding to cushion him and protect his pressure sores through take off, flight and landing. A dedicated team of Vantara veterinarians, paravets and caregivers is staying by his side for the entire journey, continuously monitoring his heart rate, breathing, temperature, hydration and blood glucose, with fluids, medication and milk feeds ready on board. Moving him by air means hours instead of days in transit, reducing stress and risk for a calf whose body has very little reserve.On arrival, Raja will be admitted to Vantara's elephant hospital, where veterinarians will carry out a full diagnostic assessment and continue pain management, medication, mobility therapy and nutritional rehabilitation. Given the nature of his injury, he is expected to need lifelong veterinary care and monitoring, and Vantara is committed to providing it. It is heartening to see Anant Ambani support the rescue of a critically ill baby elephant, enabling the calf to be airlifted to Vantara for specialised treatment and a chance at recovery.
Article Summary: Raja, an Asian elephant calf, is being airlifted from Pohumara in Assam to Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat. He suffered a complete fracture of his right femur, the large thigh bone of his hind leg, on his very first day. Raja's condition has deteriorated to a point where hospitalisation offers the only real chance of recovery.

Article Title: Owaisi-Azad alliance looks strong on paper, but Akhilesh Yadav has little to fear: 5 reasons why SP may not be worried
Article Text:
The battle for UP

I am ready to join hands. I am ready to form an alliance. Today is the time to talk. Don't cry later after the elections are over. We don't want the BJP to come to power again. Asaduddin Owaisi, AIMIM

An additional option will now be available to such innocent people who cast their votes after being misled. This will cause the BJP a loss of 2-3 per cent votes. The BJP will be left with nothing. Samajwadi Party chief, Akhilesh Yadav

Akhilesh has worked hard to change the SP's pro-Muslim image

The SP increased its tally from 17 seats in 2017 to 34 in 2022, while the BJP's count fell from 39 to 22 across 59 constituencies.

Azad's primary battle is with Mayawati

Owaisi's success in Bihar is no guarantee of success in UP

Owaisi's party won five seats in Bihar in both 2020 and 2025, but failed to win a single seat in Uttar Pradesh in 2017 and 2022.

An alliance born out of limited choices

Samajwadi Party remains the strongest challenger to the BJP

When Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad joined hands on November 12, the immediate question was whether the alliance of AIMIM and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) would become Akhilesh Yadav 's biggest worry ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.After all, the two communities they are seeking to mobilise, Muslims and Dalits, are key to Akhilesh's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak backward classes, Dalits and minorities) formula, which helped the Samajwadi Party (SP) emerge as the single-largest party in UP in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.Owaisi had been reaching out to Akhilesh for an alliance since July, even warning him not to regret rejecting the offer if the BJP returned to power. Interestingly, Owaisi was targeting the SP more than the BJP in his election meetings.Four months later, with his attempts to forge an alliance with the SP and BSP chief Mayawati yielding no results, Owaisi joined hands with Azad to form the Samajik Parivartan Morcha.Akhilesh, however, appears unfazed. He claimed the new front would cost the BJP, rather than his party, 2-3% of its votes. He also ruled out expanding the SP's existing alliance.So, is Akhilesh right in playing down the threat? Here are five reasons why the Owaisi-Azad alliance may not be as big a worry as it appears.Akhilesh Yadav has made a conscious effort to move away from the image of Muslim appeasement that the Samajwadi Party acquired under his father Mulayam Singh Yadav.While Mulayam openly flaunted Muslim voters and built his party's electoral strength around the Muslim-Yadav combination, Akhilesh has been trying to expand the SP's appeal among Hindu voters without alienating its traditional support base.From visiting temples and attending Durga Puja celebrations to hosting iftar gatherings, Akhilesh has been trying to strike a balance between the two communities.The change became particularly evident after the BJP's sweeping victory in the 2017 assembly elections, when the SP began making Akhilesh's religious engagements more public.Since then, Akhilesh has visited the Vindhyachal temple in Mirzapur and the Ravidas temple in Varanasi, installed a 51-foot statue of Lord Krishna in Saifai and initiated the construction of the Kedareshwar temple in Etawah.On December 12, Akhilesh and his wife Dimple Yadav are scheduled to make their first visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya since its consecration in January 2024.At the same time, his outreach to Muslims has continued. However, Akhilesh has been careful to avoid giving the BJP an opportunity to accuse the SP of Muslim appeasement.Joining hands with Owaisi could undo some of that work and give the BJP fresh ammunition against the SP. By rejecting an alliance with AIMIM, Akhilesh may actually be helping himself retain the broader support base he has built over the years.Chandrashekhar Azad is a leader known for taking aggressive political positions that keeps him in the news. But in Uttar Pradesh, he faces a tough challenge from Mayawati, who continues to command the support of a significant section of Dalit voters.Azad's victory from Nagina in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections established him as a Dalit leader to watch. He defeated the BJP candidate by over 1.5 lakh votes, while the SP finished a distant third and the BSP fourth.However, one Lok Sabha victory does not establish Azad as a leader of Dalits across UP. In the 2022 assembly elections, he contested against Yogi Adityanath from Gorakhpur Urban, secured fewer than 8,000 votes and lost his deposit."Jatavs, who account for around 11% of Uttar Pradesh's population, are still largely loyal to Mayawati. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, non-Jatav Dalits, particularly the Pasis, shifted towards the INDIA bloc. This played an important role in the alliance's performance," said Pravin Kumar, senior political observer and Resident Editor of TOI, Lucknow.According to the CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey, 44% of Jatav voters in UP backed the BSP in 2024, even though the party failed to win a single Lok Sabha seat.Moreover, Mayawati has brought her nephew Akash Anand back into the party and reinstated him as national convener, tasking him with expanding the BSP's appeal among young voters.Interestingly, when Mayawati removed Anand from the party in September, Azad had invited him to join the Azad Samaj Party.While Azad enjoys popularity among sections of Dalit youth, his ability to turn that popularity into votes across the state is yet to be established.AIMIM won five assembly seats each in Bihar in 2020 and 2025. However, Owaisi has struggled to make a similar impact in Uttar Pradesh."Owaisi has not been able to replicate his success in Bihar in Uttar Pradesh. The only time AIMIM made its presence felt was during the 2023 urban local body elections, when it won five chairperson seats and around 75 councillor seats. But these were just flashes of success, not signs of a larger political shift," Pravin Kumar said.In Bihar, Owaisi found a strong base in Seemanchal, a region with a large concentration of Muslim voters. All five seats won by AIMIM in both elections came from this region.In UP, however, AIMIM failed to win a single seat despite contesting 38 constituencies in 2017 and 95 in 2022. Its vote share in the last assembly elections was less than 1%.While Muslims account for around 19% of UP's population, their presence is spread across several regions. Owaisi is yet to establish a stronghold comparable to Seemanchal, while the SP enjoys considerable support among Muslim voters.Despite nearly a decade of contesting elections in UP, AIMIM is still looking for its first assembly seat.Chandrashekhar Azad was not Owaisi's first choice for an alliance in Uttar Pradesh. The AIMIM chief had repeatedly approached Akhilesh Yadav to join hands against the BJP.When the SP showed no interest, AIMIM reached out to Mayawati's Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), hoping to bring Muslims and Dalits together. However, that attempt also failed, and Owaisi eventually joined hands with Azad.But forming an alliance is one thing and getting voters to support each other's candidates is another.While Azad enjoys support among sections of Dalit youth, his ability to mobilise Dalits across the state and transfer their votes to AIMIM candidates is yet to be tested.Similarly, Owaisi will have to convince Muslim voters to back candidates fielded by Azad's party instead of the SP. For now, both Owaisi and Azad have far more to prove in the upcoming assembly elections than Akhilesh.In Uttar Pradesh, Muslim voters have largely backed parties they believe are best placed to defeat the BJP. For now, that party is the Samajwadi Party, not AIMIM.According to the CSDS-Lokniti post-poll survey, around 79% of Muslim voters backed the SP-led alliance in the 2022 assembly elections. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, 92% backed the SP-Congress alliance.The alliance won 43 of UP's 80 Lok Sabha seats, with the SP alone winning 37, compared to the BJP's 33.Akhilesh's position is also reflected in his ongoing seat-sharing negotiations with the Congress. Though the arrangement is yet to be finalised, he has made it clear that seats will be allocated based on each party's chances of winning them.While Owaisi is asking Muslims to move away from traditional political parties and build their own leadership, Akhilesh is offering them an alliance that has already demonstrated its ability to defeat the BJP.And as long as defeating the BJP remains a priority for a large section of Muslim voters in UP, convincing them to shift their support away from the SP may not be easy for Owaisi.On paper, the Owaisi-Azad alliance looks promising, with Muslims and Dalits together accounting for around 40% of UP's population. But the reality on the ground is different. Owaisi has struggled to replicate his Bihar success, while Azad is yet to establish statewide appeal. The alliance could influence closely contested seats, particularly in western UP, where Owaisi has some support.So, while the alliance may appear to be a threat to Akhilesh's PDA formula on paper, both leaders have several electoral challenges of their own to overcome.And that is perhaps why Akhilesh has little reason to be worried, at least for now.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav has made a conscious effort to move away from the image of Muslim appeasement that the Samajwadi Party acquired under his father Mulayam Singh Yadav. He has been trying to expand the SP's appeal among Hindu voters without alienating its traditional support base.

Article Title: 'His name is Siraj': Congress MP Imran Masood on why pacer wasn't picked for India vs NZ Test; BJP hits back
Article Text:
Siraj left out of India's pace attack: Congress alleges discrimination, BJP says stop dividing team

Why Siraj's exclusion has raised eyebrows

NEW DELHI: The selection of India's playing XI has triggered a face-off between the Congress and the BJP, with the opposition alleging discrimination against pacer Mohammed Siraj and the ruling party accusing it of dragging communal politics into cricket.The exchange began after India’s team management opted for a four-pronged pace attack but left out Siraj against New Zealand, despite the Hyderabad pacer’s impressive record and reputation for delivering in challenging conditions.Congress MP Imran Masood questioned Siraj’s exclusion, suggesting that his religious identity could have played a role in the decision."His name is Siraj -- isn't that reason enough? If he is performing and still not getting selected, what else could be the reason behind it? This alone can be the reason; there can be no other reason besides this," Masood told news agency IANS.In another interaction, the Congress MP said it was being pointed out that Siraj had performed well but was still not included in the team. "If you are not selecting him despite his good performance, the discrimination is clear," he told news agency ANI.The BJP was quick to hit back, accusing the Congress of turning team selection into a communal issue and using cricket for vote-bank politics.BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said, "Shame on Congress! Congress now does vote bank politics even in Cricket team selection! Congress says - 'Siraj was left out because he was a Muslim'."Pointing out that all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja had also been left out, Bhandari said, "Every cricketer wears the jersey representing India! Stop dividing Indian cricket team for vote bank and communal politics!"Siraj's omission has also drawn attention because of the role he has played in India's pace attack over the past few years.Fifteen months ago, on a cloudy morning in London, Siraj stepped out of Jasprit Bumrah's shadow to produce one of the most memorable performances of his career. The pacer emptied the tank on the final day of a gruelling five-Test series to help India secure a 2-2 draw against England at The Oval.His performance appeared to signal the beginning of a new phase in his career, with Siraj emerging as a potential leader of India's pace attack as Bumrah entered an intensive workload management programme.However, the pacer was left out on Thursday despite conditions in Wellington appearing tailor-made for seam bowling. The team management instead went ahead with four other seamers.One possible reason for the decision could be Siraj's recent form. His underwhelming performance against Sri Lanka in the Colombo Test three months ago may have prompted the team management to reassess his place in the playing XI.
Article Summary: Mohammed Siraj left out of India's pace attack against New Zealand. Congress alleges discrimination, BJP says stop dividing team for vote bank and communal politics. India's team management opted for a four-pronged pace attack but left out Siraj.

Article Title: Himalayan marmot droppings could help track climate change
Article Text:
(a, b, d): Alpine-steppe vegetation at Pensila Pass and Rimkhim; (c, e): Himalayan marmots in their natural habitats; (f, g): Marmot faeces, showing midden deposits and individual pellet morphology. | Credit: BSIP

BENGALURU: What can the droppings of a Himalayan marmot reveal about climate change? Quite a bit, according to a new study that has found pollen grains, fungal spores and elemental signatures preserved in the faeces of the high-altitude herbivore can provide clues to changing vegetation and environmental conditions in the higher Himalaya.Scientists from the Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology, explored whether marmot faeces could serve as an alternative biological archive to reconstruct environmental changes. Their findings, published in the journal PLOS One, could offer a useful tool for studying remote, arid mountain environments where conventional sources of palaeoenvironmental evidence are scarce.The Himalaya is particularly sensitive to changes in temperature, precipitation and snow cover. Such changes can affect alpine vegetation and wildlife habitats. Traditionally, scientists have relied on lake sediments, peat and soil to reconstruct past environmental conditions. The researchers sought to establish whether biological material preserved in marmot droppings could provide similar insights.The Himalayan marmot (Marmota himalayana) inhabits cold, dry alpine environments and depends on local vegetation for food and shelter. Pollen preserved in its faeces reflects the plants consumed by the animal, thereby offering a record of the surrounding alpine-steppe vegetation.The research team analysed faecal samples collected from two Himalayan regions, using pollen and fungal-spore identification, statistical methods and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (FESEM-EDS) to determine elemental composition.The analysis identified several plant groups in the marmot's diet, including Artemisia, Asteroideae, Caryophyllaceae, Poaceae, Cyperaceae and Chenopodiaceae. Researchers also examined ratios between three pollen combinations: Artemisia/Chenopodiaceae, Artemisia/Cyperaceae and Artemisia/Ephedra. These were used to interpret vegetation patterns and associated climatic conditions.The results showed that the marmot's mixed plant-based diet was dominated by groups such as Artemisia, Asteroideae, Caryophyllaceae and Chenopodiaceae, reflecting the characteristics of alpine vegetation. The researchers concluded that the Himalayan marmot could serve as an indicator species for understanding vegetation and climate changes in the higher Himalaya.The study also found that changes in marmot habitats could indicate shifts in altitude associated with changing environmental conditions. Combining pollen, fungal spores and elemental analysis could therefore provide a modern reference for future palaeoecological studies and help reconstruct past ecological changes.The findings could have implications beyond climate research. Marmots are an important prey species for snow leopards, and a better understanding of their habitat requirements could help monitor changes in the wider ecosystem and inform wildlife conservation strategies.
Article Summary: Pollen grains, fungal spores and elemental signatures preserved in the faeces of the high-altitude herbivore can provide clues to changing vegetation and environmental conditions in the higher Himalaya. The findings could offer a useful tool for studying remote, arid mountain environments where conventional sources of palaeoenvironmental evidence are scarce.

Article Title: Criticism, the price of growth
Article Text:
Kattrunai Pootti Yor Kadalil Paaychinum,

Nattrunai Aavadhu Namachivayave.

Netrikkan Thirappinum Kuttram Kuttrame

King Lear’

Arohara’

“Sevikkaippa Chorp Porukkum Panbudai Vendhan

Kavikaik Keezh Thangum Ulagu”

“The world will prosper under the umbrella of a king who has the maturity to endure words unpleasant to his ears”

The history of kings and their courtiers is replete with instances of extravagant praise . Flattery and power have shared an uncomfortable relationship for centuries. While genuine appreciation springs from admiration, sycophancy is often an investment, with the flatterer expecting favours in return. Unfortunately, the latter has always found more practitioners than the former.Tamil history and literature offer an interesting contrast. For generations, poets have shown courage in standing up to authority. Thirunavukkarasar, or Appar, faced persecution under the Pallava king Mahendravarman. Tied to a massive stone and thrown into the sea, he sang with unwavering faith:Even in the depths of the ocean, Namashivaya mantra would remain his unfailing support.Another celebrated example is Nakkeerar, who dared to challenge Lord Shiva himself. When the Lord questioned his criticism of a poem, Nakkeerar declared,– even if the third eye is opened, a fault remains a fault. His judgement would not yield, even before the divine.Yet alongside this tradition of fearless poets, there has always been another breed: those who praise rulers beyond all reasonable proportions.The phenomenon is hardly unique to Tamil history. Shakespeare’s ‘opens with a king asking his daughters to declare how much they love him. While Goneril and Regan compete in extravagant declarations, Cordelia refuses to flatter him. Lear mistakes flattery for love and truth for ingratitude.King Canute of England offers another telling anecdote. Exasperated by his courtiers’ praise, he had his throne placed by the seashore and commanded the incoming tide to stop. As the waves advanced, he demonstrated that even a king’s power had limits. Louis XIV of France cultivated a court where extravagant praise became an institution.Royal portraits followed the same tradition: imperfections were softened, stature enhanced and rulers made more majestic than reality warranted.But the responsibility for this culture does not rest entirely with those who offer praise. Much depends on the person receiving it. A leader who revels in adulation creates an environment where honest opinions become scarce.I recall an incident involving Perunthalaivar Kamarajar. At a political meeting, when a party worker began showering him with elaborate praise, Kamarajar reportedly pulled him back and asked him to get to the point instead of wasting time on eulogies. Such leaders are exceptions and not the rule.Unfortunately, the tradition of extravagant praise has only grown. Successive rulers and the artists patronised by them have seemingly competed to raise the bar of eulogy. Comparisons have become grander, language more florid and exaggeration more audacious. The culmination, in recent times, seems to be artists invoking Lord Muruga and singing ‘in praise of political leaders. A sacred invocation traditionally reserved for the deity has found an unexpected place in political adulation.Thiruvalluvar offers timeless wisdom in Kural 389: He tells the leaders to keep critics around them rather than flatterers.Perhaps the finest tribute to a leader is not the number of voices singing his praises, but the number of people who feel free to disagree. Greatness is not measured by the height of the pedestal on which admirers place a ruler, but by his willingness to remain grounded.
Article Summary: The history of kings and their courtiers is replete with instances of extravagant praise. Flattery and power have shared an uncomfortable relationship for centuries. While genuine appreciation springs from admiration, sycophancy is often an investment. A leader who revels in adulation creates an environment where honest opinions become scarce.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court 's registry came under an unflattering spotlight Friday with a bench led by the CJI smelling a rat in Enforcement Directorate 's appeal challenging grant of bail to an accused in a money laundering case not getting listed for three years. It ordered SC's top administrative officer to conduct a thorough inquiry into the reasons behind the registry consigning a live case to cold storage.Finding that ED's appeal against bail to Raman Singhal was last listed in Sept 2023, when the court had issued notice to the accused, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "What is that great magic wand that was used by someone by which the case was not listed for hearing for three years?"It added, "It was directed to be listed in Sept 2023. Sept 2024, Sept 2025 and Sept 2026 have gone by and the matter did not get listed. Who managed it? The registry must explain this lapse." Senior advocate Sidharth Dave said no one could manage listing in SC as it was computer-based but the bench said, "What other inference can we draw from the non-listing?"The bench directed secretary general Ajit Atri to carry out an inquiry and file a report explaining why ED's petition was not listed."It seems that the listing branch (of the registry) would have continued to not list the appeal but for our Nov 4 order," the bench said.Though the court ordered an inquiry into the non-listing of the matter, it disposed of the appeal and said it would not entertain a challenge to bail granted more than three years ago, especially after ED counsel Zoheb Hossain informed SC that the trial in the case had already commenced and eight witnesses had been examined.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate's appeal challenging grant of bail to an accused in a money laundering case not getting listed for three years. The bench ordered SC's top administrative officer to conduct a thorough inquiry into the reasons behind the registry consigning a live case to cold storage.

Article Title: Indian Team leaves for Bangladesh for talks on Ganga water
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A four-member team from India headed to Bangladesh Friday to attend a meeting of the joint committee constituted under Ganga Water Treaty between the two countries to monitor the sharing of the river's waters. The meeting is scheduled for Nov 21-23.The visit comes weeks before the 30-year-old treaty is due to lapse on Dec 12, even as the team, led by head of India's Joint Rivers Commission Sharad Chandra, visiting Dhaka doesn't have the mandate to discuss the agreement's extension beyond its existing term.Sources hinted that it is for the political leadership of both nations to take a call on its renewal or interim extension and its terms, whatever the case may be. Bangladesh has said instead of renewing the existing one, it wants to negotiate a new treaty with India, including a clause guaranteeing that its required share of water during the dry season is protected.

Article Title: Ex-IAF vice-chief slams UK report claiming India has 32 Rafales instead of 36 as 'patently false'

Air Marshal Narmdeshwar Tiwari (retd), who played active roles during the Kargil war and Operation Sindoor.

NEW DELHI: A former Indian Air Force vice-chief has debunked a controversial report by a British aviation magazine that listed four fewer Rafale fighter jets in the IAF’s fleet, showing just 32 aircraft as compared to 36 India had acquired from France. Air Marshal Narmdeshwar Tiwari (retd), who played active roles during the Kargil war and Operation Sindoor in May last year, called FlightGlobal’s figures “patently false”.FlightGlobal’s latest World Air Forces directory report has neither given any explanation nor provided any evidence for the reduced number of Rafale jets with the IAF. Under the ‘India’ head, the report just showed the ‘active’ number of Rafale jets as 32 and showed 114 such 4.5-generation fighter jets under the category ‘ordered’ which India is planning to acquire from France after signing a formal contract. Even in its last year’s report, published months after Op Sindoor, FlightGlobal had listed 35 active Rafales, one aircraft fewer than the actual number.Air Marshal Tiwari (retd) questioned the credibility of the aviation magazine’s sources. “FlightGlobal should re-evaluate their sources. The same sources gave specific tail numbers, which since have been flying in various exercises including international ones.The same sources said that Sqn Ldr Shivangi Singh was taken as a prisoner of war (PoW). We all know how that turned out,” Air Marshal Tiwari, who retired last year in Dec after Op Sindoor, posted on X on Thursday night.Pakistani media outlets and pro-Pakistan social media handles had then said that Sqn Ldr Shivangi was held hostage as a PoW. After the conflict, a smiling Shivangi had posed with President Droupadi Murmu at Ambala airbase, debunking claims of her being held hostage by Pakistan as a PoW.In June this year, an IAF tender sought ‘bridge support’ (maintenance) for all 36 Rafale fighter jets, contradicting Pakistan’s repeated claims that India had lost several Rafale jets during Op Sindoor. Though Indian military leadership had repeatedly rubbished such claims, Pakistan kept insisting that it had downed several multi-role Rafale fighters during the conflict.Last year in June, Dassault Aviation CEO Éric Trappier called Pakistan’s claims of shooting down IAF’s Rafale jets “inaccurate”, while noting that Indian authorities had not communicated details of any Rafale losses.
Article Summary: FlightGlobal’s latest World Air Forces directory report has neither given any explanation nor provided any evidence for the reduced number of Rafale jets with the IAF. Air Marshal Narmdeshwar Tiwari (retd), who played active roles during the Kargil war and Operation Sindoor, called the figures ‘patently false’

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: Tom Brady targets $4.2 billion football team ownership stake after Birmingham City exit as seven-time Super Bowl champion expands sports empire

Tom Brady may be preparing for another major move in English football, and this time, the spotlight is on Chelsea. The seven-time Super Bowl champion has reportedly opened discussions about purchasing a minority stake in the London club, just days after ending his involvement with Birmingham City. The potential investment could mark a significant shift in Brady's football ambitions, particularly given his growing connections with influential figures in the sport. Although no agreement has been confirmed, his reported interest has already raised questions about his next chapter as a sports investor.According to a report by The Guardian published on November 20, Brady is exploring the possibility of becoming a minority investor at Chelsea. His departure from Birmingham City earlier this month has added weight to the speculation, with sources suggesting that the decision could have cleared the way for a move to Stamford Bridge.Brady's relationship with Chelsea's ownership group could prove important in these discussions. The former NFL quarterback reportedly shares a good relationship with Behdad Eghbali, whose investment firm, Clearlake Capital, now controls 86.5% of the Premier League club.Chelsea's ownership structure changed significantly in September after Todd Boehly and Mark Walter sold their shares, leaving Clearlake with full control. That development could create a different investment landscape for potential minority stakeholders.Brady is also no stranger to the club. He attended Chelsea's Club World Cup celebrations in New Jersey last year, when the English side defeated Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the final. His presence among the players offered an early glimpse of his connection with the club.Chelsea has declined to comment on the reported discussions.Brady's possible Chelsea move comes after a three-year association with Birmingham City. He invested in the club in August 2023, following its takeover by Tom Wagner's Knighthead Capital, and became chair of its advisory board.His involvement extended beyond ownership. Brady featured prominently in the 2025 Amazon Prime documentary, which offered viewers a look at his approach to football management. One memorable moment came when he questioned former manager Wayne Rooney's work ethic, sparking a public response from the ex-England captain.Birmingham acknowledged Brady's contribution when announcing his exit, stating: “Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years.”However, Birmingham is not the only sporting investment in Brady's portfolio. He also owns a minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, having purchased it alongside Wagner.A potential Chelsea investment would further strengthen his presence in professional sports beyond American football. For now, the discussions remain at an early stage, but Brady's next business move could bring one of the NFL's biggest names closer to the heart of English football.
Article Summary: Tom Brady has reportedly opened discussions about purchasing a minority stake in Chelsea. The potential investment could mark a significant shift in Brady's football ambitions. The former NFL quarterback ended his involvement with Birmingham City earlier this month. Chelsea has declined to comment on the reported discussions.

Article Title: Rockstar's GTA 6 shatters entertainment launch records with a first-day haul that dwarfs GTA 5
Article Text:
GTA 6. Image via: Rockstar Games

How big is GTA 6 's launch compared with past entertainment records?

Early reviews, server traffic and the cast behind Vice City

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Grand Theft Auto VI made $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, Rockstar Games said Friday, the biggest entertainment launch ever recorded. The figure covers worldwide sales through the end of Nov. 19, the day the game went on sale, and comes from company estimates. Rockstar also said 32.5 million copies sold before release. GTA V, the old record holder, made $815.7 million in its first 24 hours back in 2013. GTA VI cleared that mark more than four times over. Exactly how much came from pre-orders and how much from launch day is not clear yet.Rockstar called the total a record for entertainment across any medium, and the comparisons back it up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day, this year's top-grossing film so far, made $2.5 billion across its entire run in cinemas. GTA 6 passed that in one day.Outside estimates had not come close. Trackers put GTA 6 at 19.1 million copies and about $1.84 billion by launch morning, well below what Rockstar reported. GTA V's 24-hour mark of 11.21 million copies had stood since 2013.Rockstar president and founder Sam Houser said, “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world.”The standard edition costs $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99. About three quarters of sales are on PlayStation 5, with the rest on Xbox. The series has now sold nearly 480 million units, and GTA V alone is near 235 million.The critics have been kind. GTA 6 holds a 99 Metascore, tying Ocarina of Time for the best mark on Metacritic. IGN called it an “uncompromisingly engineered” masterpiece. Players are less sure, with a user score of 5.0 out of 10 from nearly 4,000 ratings on Friday afternoon.The rush showed up online too. Traffic data had PS5 downloads in the UK peaking at 8.6 times normal levels around launch, and Rockstar's online services hit 11.2 times normal in Australia. New Zealand, where the game arrived first, jumped 14.8-fold four hours earlier, which suggests some players switched regions for early access. The 212GB file also broke Virgin Media O2's evening traffic record.Japan has censored parts of the game for its graphic content, and like earlier entries it is not approved for sale in mainland China. Police departments in the US also reminded players that street racing, auto theft and gun violence are still crimes.Rockstar has also named the cast. Manni L. Perez plays Lucia, Dylan Rourke plays Jason, and NFL star Tyreek Hill voices wide receiver Maleek Rivers. No date is set yet for a PC release or the multiplayer expansion.
Article Summary: Grand Theft Auto VI made $3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, Rockstar Games said. The figure covers worldwide sales through the end of Nov. 19, the day the game went on sale. The old record holder, GTA V, made $815.7 million in its first 24 hours back in 2013.

Article Title: Sam Hartman plans to study The Bachelor like NFL game film after admitting he has never watched an episode
Article Text:
Sam Hartman's Unexpected Preparation for His New Bachelor Role (Disney)

Sam Hartman plans to study The Bachelor like game film

The Commanders quarterback says he wants to be himself

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sam Hartman has spent years preparing for football games by studying film, but his next assignment calls for different homework. The Washington Commanders quarterback, set to lead the next season of ABC’s The Bachelor, admitted he has never watched an episode of the long-running dating show. Hartman told reporters on Thursday, Nov. 19, that he plans to catch up after the NFL regular season, using the same detailed approach he brings to the field. Until then, he says, football remains his priority.“I haven’t seen an episode,” Hartman said after the Commanders’ Thursday practice, referring to all 29 seasons of The Bachelor. That leaves the 27-year-old with plenty of viewing to do before filming begins after the NFL regular season.He plans to use the tools he knows best. “I’m going to probably do some tape-watching after the season is over and study up,” Hartman said. He described the plan in football terms: “get the DVSport clicker going, you know, kind of break down first down, second down, third down and finally end at the fantasy suite.”Hartman sees the programme as more than a TV detour. He called it “an exciting opp to showcase who I am on TV” and said he hopes to find “my future teammate for life.”Asked whether love can come from a reality show, Hartman said yes. He turned the question back on the reporter before making his point: “no matter how you meet somebody,” what matters is whether you want to be with that person.Hartman has been open about the nerves that come with the assignment. His casting was announced during a live appearance on Good Morning America on Nov. 13. Asked how he felt, he replied: “[I’m] very nervous,” before adding, “I have a tough time holding a conversation with one girl; 30 is gonna be pretty tough.”He told reporters that he had informed his Commanders teammates about the show around two weeks before the announcement. “Respect to my teammates for keeping it on the down low,” he said. Their reactions have included “a lot of really, really bad advice and some good advice.”Hartman did not identify the bad suggestions. The useful guidance was to enjoy the experience and remain authentic. He said putting on a front would be the worst approach, particularly with so many people watching.His idea of a suitable partner comes back to values. Hartman said his mother is a nurse and that he hopes to meet someone who “has a lot of compassion and shares that kind of love for giving back to people, and ultimately giving back to each other.”He has said he is “super-focused on football” until the season ends. Former NFL players Rob Gronkowski and Julian Edelman have questioned the timing of his Bachelor promotion during the season, but Hartman says football comes first. He wants to finish the season before turning to the cameras.Hartman knows the show will bring scrutiny, much as his career has brought praise and criticism. His aim is to find a lasting relationship rather than simply make television. He joked that he hopes to find a second love while continuing to show that person his first love: football.

Article Title: Daniel Jones' nearly $167 million NFL fortune reveals how much he has earned despite uncertainty surrounding his career
Article Text:
Daniel Jones has been released by Colts (Image via Getty Images)

Daniel Jones' nearly $167 million NFL fortune and what it says about his career

Jones' Colts contract left a $49.8 million bill for a 3-8 season

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Daniel Jones has been waived by the Indianapolis Colts, but his bank account is in good shape. Over The Cap lists his career NFL earnings at $166.9 million across stints with the Giants, Vikings and Colts. The Colts released him on Friday, one day after a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and an interception before Anthony Richardson took over. Richardson will start against the New York Giants on Nov. 29. At 29, Jones now faces an open question about where he plays next.Jones was the sixth overall pick in the 2019 draft, and the Giants gave him a four-year rookie deal worth $25.66 million. After the 2022 season, New York raised the stakes with a four-year, $160 million extension.Headlines said $160 million. The cash said otherwise. The Giants moved on after two seasons, and Over The Cap puts his earnings under that extension at about $46 million. Then came the part many fans forget. Spotrac says New York paid him another $36 million in 2024 after waiving him that November.Minnesota was a short stop. Indianapolis was the reset. Jones signed a one-year, $14 million deal for 2025 and threw for 3,101 yards, 19 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 13 games.It was one of the most productive years of his career, and the Colts paid for it with a two-year, $88 million contract. Nearly $50 million was fully guaranteed, and incentives could lift the value to $100 million.Add the $160 million and the $88 million and you get $248 million. That is not what Jones earned. His career has had more swings than most, and two teams have now cut him. Each exit still came with real money.This season went the other way. Jones went 3-8 as the starter, with 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions. Spotrac says the Colts will have paid about $49.8 million for his work in 2026. That is a steep bill for a quarterback who lost his job during a losing year.The guarantees explain why. With nearly $50 million fully guaranteed, benching or cutting him did not erase what the Colts owed.Dead cap is where it lingers. Indianapolis is projected to carry $14.89 million for Jones in 2026 and $35.2 million in 2027. Those are cap accounting figures, not new payments to him.Football is only part of the picture. Forbes lists Nike, FedEx, Amazon Data Centers, Fanatics, Hugo Boss, Panini, Raising Cane's, United Airlines and Verizon among his sponsors. The value of those deals is not public, so the NFL total should not be treated as his net worth.Jones is 29, and another contract is possible. Teams will weigh his 2025 numbers against this year's. Whether anyone wants him as a starter is the unanswered part. The money, at least, is settled.
Article Summary: Daniel Jones' career NFL earnings at $166.9 million across stints with the Giants, Vikings and Colts. The Colts released him on Friday, one day after a 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards and an interception before Anthony Richardson took over.

Article Title: Bengaluru woman undergoes D&C after failed twin pregnancy, suffers weeks of blood loss and needs 2 more procedures in Madurai; consumer commission holds doctor negligent, orders Rs 2 lakh compensation
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





BENGALURU: A procedure meant to clear her uterus after a failed pregnancy was supposed to end her ordeal. Instead, a woman kept bleeding for weeks and eventually needed a third procedure and a blood transfusion in another city. The Bangalore I Additional District Consumer Commission has now held the doctor negligent.The ordeal began on Oct 8, 2024, when Amrutha (name changed), a resident of Kalena Agrahara, visited Shree Krishna Clinic in JP Nagar 8th Phase for a pregnancy test. On Dr Shailaja N’s advice, she underwent a scan that revealed no heartbeat in her eight-week twin pregnancy, which was diagnosed as a failed pregnancy. The doctor recommended dilatation and curettage (D&C) and referred her to Rainbow Children’s Hospital, Billekahalli, where she worked as a consultant.Amrutha was admitted the next day and underwent D&C under general anaesthesia. Hospital records stated that the products of conception were removed and her post-operative recovery was uneventful. She was discharged the same day after paying Rs 37,982 and Rs 5,000.However, the bleeding worsened, leaving her in severe pain and making her pale and unstable. When she returned on Oct 14, her haemoglobin levels had dropped drastically, but she alleged that the doctor prescribed only medicines.On Oct 19, she was told that blood clots remained in her uterus and underwent a second D&C at the clinic. She alleged that the procedure was performed without anaesthesia or life support, causing “deadly” pain and violating standard medical protocols. She said she paid for all the treatment and medicines.With the bleeding and pain continuing, she travelled to her mother’s home in Madurai. Tests there revealed retained products of conception, following which she underwent a third D&C. The ordeal left her traumatised, weak and anxious. She had also suffered severe blood loss and required a transfusion.On Diwali, her haemoglobin levels dropped drastically again, prompting her admission to Aristo Specialty Hospital, Madurai. Doctors performed manual vacuum aspiration under intravenous anaesthesia and diagnosed retained products of conception and acute menorrhagia (heavy bleeding). She was discharged on Nov 1 after paying Rs 39,420.Amrutha alleged that she had been treated “like a lab rat” and that the doctor had failed to properly diagnose and treat her condition and ensure adequate care.After a legal notice sent in January 2025 drew a reply she found untenable, Amrutha filed a consumer complaint on March 21, alleging mental trauma.In their defence, Rainbow Children’s Hospital said the risks had been explained and consent obtained before the procedure. It maintained that Amrutha was stable, was shifted to the ward after stabilisation and was discharged the same day. It added that she never returned to the hospital and that her legal notice did not allege negligence. The clinic and Dr Shailaja appeared through counsel but did not file their defence despite being given sufficient opportunity.The commission noted that the clinic and doctor had failed to rebut Amrutha’s evidence. It held that she had to undergo three D&C procedures because the first had not been performed properly, eventually forcing her to seek treatment in Madurai. It also faulted the doctor for performing the second procedure at her clinic instead of referring her to a specialised hospital. The commission held that this violated standard medical protocols and amounted to medical negligence and deficiency in service.The bench, comprising president Syed Anser Kaleem and members Jyothi N and Renukadevi Deshpande, directed the clinic and Dr Shailaja to pay Rs 2 lakh as compensation and Rs 2,000 towards litigation costs. The complaint against Rainbow Children’s Hospital was dismissed.
Article Summary: Woman kept bleeding for weeks and eventually needed a third procedure and a blood transfusion in another city. Bangalore I Additional District Consumer Commission has now held the doctor negligent. The ordeal began on Oct 8, 2024, when Amrutha (name changed) visited Shree Krishna Clinic in JP Nagar 8th Phase for a pregnancy test.

Article Title: Gill misses century by two runs: Jacob Duffy ends Shubman's innings on 98 in last over of day 3
Article Text:
Shubman Gill

Rahul's 136, Gill's 98 guide India to 486/4 against NZ on Day 3
