India captain Shubman Gill missed a century by just two runs after being bowled by Jacob Duffy in the final over of Day 3 of the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington on Saturday.Batting on 98, Gill was looking to reach his hundred before the close of play when Duffy got a delivery to move back in and breach his defence. The ball struck Gill's pad before deflecting onto the off stump, ending his innings and leaving him short of the milestone.Gill's dismissal came after he and Rishabh Pant had added 100 runs for the fourth wicket. Pant remained unbeaten on 55 at stumps, with nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj at the other end.India finished the day at 486/4 in 125 overs, taking a lead of 118 runs after New Zealand had scored 368 in their first innings. KL Rahul led the batting effort with 136, his 13th Test century, while Devdutt Padikkal contributed 80 off 175 balls.Rahul and Padikkal added 165 runs for the second wicket before Kyle Jamieson dismissed the left-hander. Rahul then shared a 91-run stand with Gill before Nathan Smith ended his innings. Rahul struck nine fours and two sixes, while Gill hit the same number of boundaries and sixes in his 98-run knock.On Friday, New Zealand had posted 368 in their first innings, with Henry Nicholls scoring an unbeaten 175.
Article Summary: India captain Shubman Gill bowled by Jacob Duffy in final over of Day 3. Gill was looking to reach his hundred before the close of play. India finished the day at 486/4 in 125 overs, taking a lead of 118 runs. New Zealand had scored 368 in their first innings.

Article Title: Who is fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series? Cody Rhodes and CM Punk find their pick on SmackDown
Article Text:
CM Punk and Cody Rhodes. Image via: WWE

Who is the fifth member of Team USA at Survivor Series?

Team USA's lineup and the Priest attack on Williams

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Trick Williams is the fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series: WarGames. Cody Rhodes and CM Punk settled the spot on the November 20 SmackDown in Evansville, Indiana. Punk had first put forward Hacksaw Jim Duggan, Rhodes pushed back, and Duggan then said no himself. The United States Champion came out with Lil Yachty, made his own case, and got the nod. Team USA will face Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico on November 28 in Houston. The show ended with word backstage from Nick Aldis that Williams was hurt.Trick Williams got the spot after a detour. Rhodes had told Aldis he would name the pick that night, but Rey Fenix then reported that Punk was already heading to the ring. Punk opened the segment by presenting Hall of Famer Hacksaw Jim Duggan as his pick, and Rhodes was not sold. They went back and forth until Rhodes gave in. A video package on Team Mexico then aired, and Duggan changed his mind. He asked if they still wanted him in the match, said no and left the ring.Williams came out next with Lil Yachty, with Rhodes and Punk still in the ring. Yachty argued the United States Champion deserved a place on Team USA, and the two leaders agreed. All four hugged. Duggan was the sentimental pick. Williams is the practical one, because a champion is a built-in argument. WWE announced the decision online soon after. "Team USA with the United States Champion?!" the post from @WWE said. It went on: "As agreed upon by @CodyRhodes and @CMPunk, @_trickwilliams is the 5th Member of Team USA for Survivor Series!"Williams then wrestled Damian Priest, with Yachty at ringside. Priest landed early right hands, but Williams answered with a neckbreaker and a clothesline that sent Priest over the top rope to the floor. Williams then threw Priest into the announce table. As Williams set up a big boot, Priest grabbed the ring bell and hit him with it. The referee called for the bell, and Williams won by disqualification.Priest was not done. He hit Williams again after the match, and WWE officials came out to pull them apart. Backstage, Aldis told Rhodes and Punk that Williams is hurt. Both were angry. How serious the injury is has not been made clear, and the spot is not safe until WWE says more.Team USA now has Rhodes, Punk, LA Knight, Je'Von Evans and Williams. Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico has Mysterio, Penta, Rey Fenix and Dragon Lee, with the fifth name still to come. Fenix was on the SmackDown card too, booked against Kit Wilson.
Article Summary: Trick Williams is the fifth and final member of Team USA for Survivor Series: WarGames. Cody Rhodes and CM Punk settled the spot on the November 20 SmackDown. Team USA will face Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico on November 28 in Houston.

Article Title: Myles Garrett carries his late friend's memory into every game as emotional 'Live Like Luke' tribute honours the college teammate he lost to cancer
Article Text:
Myles Garrett (Getty Images)

Myles Garrett's wristband keeps his late friend close every day

Luke Laufenberg's cancer battle left a lasting impact on Myles Garrett

Myles Garrett honours Luke Laufenberg with emotional cleats tribute

Luke Laufenberg Fight Fund turns his memory into support for others

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Myles Garrett, one of the most meaningful things he carries onto a football field is not a helmet, a trophy or a piece of protective equipment. It is a small blue wristband bearing the words “Live Like Luke. ” The Cleveland Browns star wears it every day to remember Luke Laufenberg, his former Texas A&M teammate who died at 21 after battling an aggressive form of cancer. Their time together ended far too soon, but Garrett has never allowed that friendship to become just a memory. Through personal tributes and charitable support, he continues to share the story of a young man whose outlook on life left a lasting mark on him.Some friendships leave a mark that time cannot erase. For Garrett, Luke's place in his life is reflected in a simple ritual that has stayed with him long after their college days ended.“This wristband is on 24/7,” Garrett said, describing the blue band that carries Luke's name and message. It is not something he wears only during games or special occasions. The wristband remains a constant reminder of the person behind it.The two met at Texas A&M, where Garrett was already making a name for himself as a powerful defensive player. Luke, meanwhile, joined the football programme as a walk-on tight end. His role often put him on the opposite side of Garrett during practice, where he had to block the future NFL star on the scout team.Their positions may have been different, but football gave them a chance to build a friendship. Garrett remembers more than the time they spent on the field. He remembers Luke's willingness to help people and his habit of putting others first.“He was always asking me, ‘What do you need? I’ll do that, I’ll be that,’” Garrett recalled.That question offers a glimpse into the kind of person Luke was. He did not need a big platform to make a difference. He simply looked for ways to support the people around him. Garrett has carried that lesson with him, turning a personal reminder into a way to encourage others to live with the same generosity.Luke's life changed in 2017, when he was diagnosed with Burkitt lymphoma, a rare and aggressive form of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. He was only 19. The diagnosis came just months after he had celebrated Garrett's selection by the Cleveland Browns as the first overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft.The illness brought a difficult fight, but Luke continued to show the spirit that had drawn people towards him. His battle lasted less than two years. He died in 2019, aged 21, leaving his family, teammates and friends to deal with a loss that came far too early.For Garrett, remembering Luke means looking beyond the illness and the painful circumstances of his death. He wants people to know the person who lived with courage, optimism and a desire to make others better.That is why the words “Live Like Luke” carry so much meaning. They are not simply a slogan printed on a wristband. They reflect the qualities Garrett saw in his friend and wants others to carry into their own lives.“Optimistic, resilient, just always wanted to be the one percent better, make people around him a little bit better just for knowing him and that wasn't his goal or mission but just the kind of person he was. I think we all could live like that,” Garrett said.Luke's approach to life also gives Garrett a different way to measure success. Football offers records, awards and public recognition. But the influence one person has on others can last much longer than a season. Luke's example continues to shape how Garrett thinks about friendship, kindness and responsibility.Garrett found another way to make Luke's story visible during the NFL's My Cause My Cleats campaign in November 2025. The initiative gives players an opportunity to use custom footwear to highlight causes that matter to them.Garrett chose the Luke Laufenberg Fight Fund. His cleats featured Luke's portrait against a blue, sky-inspired background, along with the hashtag #LiveLikeLuke. The design brought a deeply personal story onto a national football stage.The tribute also gave Garrett a chance to reconnect with memories from college. He had met Jason Garrett and shared a photograph with him, which brought back emotions from the time he spent with Luke. The moment helped inspire his decision to make the tribute more visible.“Well, I got the chance to meet with Jason Garrett, and we took a picture and sent it to Babe, and kind of brought back that emotion back of that time when we were in college and we were spending time on the field, time after school and after practice together, just bringing back those memories. I always wear his wristband, reminding me of and the kind of person that he is.”Garrett also explained why he wanted to bring Luke's story to a wider audience.“I just wanted to bring it full circle and show how much he left an impression on all of us, including myself and he's a hell of a person and I'm better because I knew him,” Garrett said.The cleats meant more than a visual tribute. They gave fans a chance to learn about a young athlete whose life had touched one of the NFL's biggest defensive stars. They also helped direct attention towards a cause that carries Luke's name.The most meaningful part of Garrett's tribute may be the work that continues beyond the football field. The Luke Laufenberg Fight Fund was established in Luke's honour at the University of Texas at El Paso. It supports student-athletes who share the qualities that defined him, including determination, generosity and a willingness to help others.The fund gives Garrett a way to turn remembrance into practical support. Instead of allowing Luke's story to remain limited to old photographs and memories, the initiative helps provide resources for young athletes who are building their own futures.Garrett has also spoken about how Luke's habit of looking out for others could inspire a wider change in everyday life.“Luke was always reaching out and seeing what another person needed,” Garrett said. “If everyone did that, the world would be a much better place.”That message is at the heart of the #LiveLikeLuke tribute. It asks people to notice those around them, offer help when they can and make an effort to leave others better than they found them.For Garrett, the wristband remains the most personal part of the tribute. The custom cleats brought Luke's face before a much larger audience, while the fund helps keep his values active in the lives of young athletes.A football career is often measured by what a player achieves on the field. Garrett's tribute tells another story. It shows how a friendship can continue to influence someone long after a final practice or game. Luke Laufenberg did not get the chance to see where life would take his college teammate, but his spirit remains part of Garrett's journey.Every time Garrett looks at that blue wristband, he has a reminder of what truly matters. And every time he shares Luke's story, he gives others a reason to remember him, too.
Article Summary: Cleveland Browns star Myles Garrett wears Luke Laufenberg's wristband 24/7. Luke was his former Texas A&M teammate who died at 21 after battling an aggressive form of cancer. Garrett wants people to know the person who lived with courage, optimism and a desire to make others better.

Article Title: Another fifty, another statement! Devdutt Padikkal strengthens No.3 claim: 'Always great to get some runs'
Article Text:
Devdutt Padikkal (Pic credit: BCCI)

Rahul partnership key to keeping New Zealand at bay

Padikkal focused on extending India's lead

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India's search for a dependable number three in Test cricket could finally be yielding results, with Devdutt Padikkal strengthening his case for the crucial position through another composed half-century against New Zealand in the first Test in Wellington.The left-hander scored a patient 80 off 175 deliveries, helping India take control of the contest after New Zealand posted 368 in their first innings. Padikkal shared a crucial 165-run partnership with KL Rahul (136), ensuring India did not allow the hosts to claw their way back into the match on the third day.India reached 486/4 at stumps, establishing a 118-run lead with two days remaining. For Padikkal, it was another significant contribution in a promising start to his Test career, having now registered four scores of fifty or more in seven innings across five matches."It's always great to get some runs," Padikkal said after the day's play. "It was important that me and KL (Rahul) started off the day well. It was important that we didn't let them back into the game, and I think we did that pretty well today."Resuming at 159/1 on Day 3, Rahul and Padikkal ensured India negotiated the morning session without losing a wicket. The Karnataka batter said surviving that crucial period was central to their partnership and India's subsequent dominance."Yeah, like I said, it was important that we got through that first session. I think if they were able to pick up a couple of wickets early, it would have put us in a bit of a difficult position," he explained."But I think that was the conversation, just building that partnership and taking it as deep as possible. And once we were able to do that, then it was our turn to put pressure back on them. And I think we did that well."Padikkal reached his half-century off 98 balls before continuing to build on the partnership. His innings eventually ended when Kyle Jamieson produced a delivery that straightened and clipped the top of off stump.The 26-year-old also spoke about his first experience of playing in New Zealand, admitting that the conditions at the Basin Reserve were different from what the Indian batters had anticipated."Yeah, it's a great ground. It's my first time in New Zealand. I really enjoyed being out here and this was a great venue to play cricket at. And hopefully we can continue to play some good cricket and get a win with us," he said.Padikkal revealed that India had expected more assistance for the seamers from the surface but had found the pitch considerably flatter than anticipated."Yeah, definitely. I think we expected a lot, a lot of grass on the wicket. We expected a lot of movement. It's probably not panned out that way. It's been much flatter than we expected. But at the same time, it's important that you respect the conditions that are in front of you."He added: "I think it was important that we continue to score big. And that's the conversation in the dressing room as well. Everyone's really confident. Everyone's had a lot of preparation behind them coming into this Test match and that shows."Padikkal, who made his Test debut in 2024, established himself as a contender for the number three position when India gave him the opportunity during the Sri Lanka series earlier this year.In five Tests and seven innings, he has accumulated 498 runs at an impressive average of 71.14, including two centuries and two half-centuries. His latest contribution in Wellington further strengthens his credentials as India look to settle their top order.With India already holding a substantial lead, Padikkal stressed that the focus was on building an even bigger advantage rather than looking too far ahead."Not yet. We are not looking too far ahead. It's important that we take one session at a time. I think definitely we are in a really good position right now. But it's important that we really extend that lead as much as possible so that we can put more pressure on them."India will resume Day 4 with six wickets in hand, looking to build on their advantage and put New Zealand under further pressure.
Article Summary: Devdutt Padikkal scores 80 as India reach 486-4 on Day 3 of first Test in Wellington. Left-hander has now scored four scores of fifty or more in seven innings. India lead New Zealand by 118 runs with two days remaining.

Article Title: Luka Doncic gets a major Kareem Abdul-Jabbar endorsement as Lakers' post-LeBron era takes shape
Article Text:
Luka Doncic. Image via: Harry How/ Getty Images

Why did Kareem Abdul-Jabbar pick Luka Doncic to lead the post-LeBron Lakers?

Luka Doncic. Image via: Adam Pantozzi/National Basketball Association via Getty Images

Kessler and Redick back Doncic on defense

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lakers legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar has publicly cleared Luka Doncic to take over the franchise from LeBron James . In a Substack column, Abdul-Jabbar told worried fans to relax after James left for Philadelphia. Los Angeles sits at 13-3 with ten new players, and Doncic leads the NBA at 38.1 points per game through 14 appearances. Teammate Walker Kessler added his own support this week, pushing back on the idea that Doncic is a poor defender. The Lakers’ nine-game winning streak ended with a 109-97 loss to Utah, yet Abdul-Jabbar saw little reason to worry.Abdul-Jabbar wrote that few people expected much from the Lakers this year. James had left, ten new players had arrived, and matching last season’s 53 wins looked like a heavy lift, even with Doncic and Austin Reaves back in the backcourt.Los Angeles went 13-3 anyway. After the Jazz ended the streak, Abdul-Jabbar kept his message simple. “Luka has shown he’s more than ready to wear the crown,” he wrote.The praise matters because Abdul-Jabbar picks his spots. He and Magic Johnson built the 1980s Lakers into the league’s top franchise during the rivalry with Boston, and Kobe Bryant, Shaquille O’Neal and James kept the team relevant after them.The pressure on Doncic has only grown. His trade from Dallas stunned the league, and the Slovenian star’s first Los Angeles postseason ended in a first-round loss to Minnesota.Then James, Rui Hachimura and other starters left. Doncic has responded by lifting a reshaped roster to an elite early record.The production backs the praise. Doncic is adding 7.0 rebounds and 7.6 assists to the scoring, and the Lakers are doing it with a roster few people picked to match last year’s 53 wins.Kessler has heard the criticism and does not buy it. On The Old Man and The Three podcast, the center called Doncic “a better defender than a lot of people think.” He pointed to Doncic’s work in passing lanes and on help-side rotations, and called him very smart.The numbers back Kessler up. The six-time All-Star averages 1.9 steals and 0.6 blocks, and opponents have shot 37.7 percent on attempts he defends. Against Toronto on Nov. 1, Doncic piled up 45 points, 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals and a block in a 131-125 win. It ranks among his most complete games of the year. Coach JJ Redick has also praised Doncic’s positioning, communication, and activity inside the defensive scheme.The MVP award is the next target. Doncic reached the Finals with Kyrie Irving in Dallas but has never come close to the award, and winning it would put him on a list with Abdul-Jabbar, Johnson, Bryant and O’Neal. Reaves, Kessler, and the rotating wing defenders fit well beside him.
Article Summary: Lakers legend Kareem Abdul-Jabbar has publicly cleared Luka Doncic to take over the franchise from LeBron James. The Slovenian star leads the NBA at 38.1 points per game through 14 appearances. Teammate Walker Kessler added his own support this week, pushing back on the idea that doncic is a poor defender.

Article Title: Dianna Russini has no plans to spill the details as tell-all book rumors force a public response
Article Text:
Dianna Russini. Image via: Getty Images

Is Dianna Russini writing a tell-all book?

Dianna Russini (Getty Images)

Thom Brennaman defends Russini after backlash over her return

Dianna Russini is not writing a tell-all book, according to TMZ. Sources close to the sports reporter say offers have poured in since Russini left The Athletic, but no pages are being written. The denial answers a claim Boston radio host Jim Murray made Friday on 98.5 The Sports Hub. Murray said a friend of his spoke with Russini at Teddy Atlas’s annual dinner in New York on Thursday night and was told a book is coming. So far, the word has come from people around her, not from Russini.No, according to people close to her. Sources told TMZ that the NFL reporter has fielded offers of all kinds since the scandal involving Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, yet nothing is being written. Her focus is getting back to the reporting she loves.The rumor began on the radio. Murray told co-hosts Michael Felger and Tony Massarotti that Russini will be “talking about everything that’s gone on,” at least as his friend heard it. He also floated the idea that Vrabel may already know what is coming.Russini was at the dinner. A photo gallery from the 30th Annual Teddy Dinner in Staten Island shows her there. The book claim itself rests on a secondhand account from an unnamed friend.A tell-all has been floated for a while as a way for Russini to give her side. She left The Athletic on April 14 and has said little in public since. Before her new show launched, she told People “the lies became so out of control,” but gave no details on what they were.Brennaman spoke on the Awful Announcing Podcast, in remarks published Nov. 19. A slur he said on an open mic ended his Reds and Fox Sports work, and he now hosts mornings on WLW. He said plenty of people are judging Russini for coming back too soon, though most do not know what the situation really was. Who gets to decide when someone can go back to earning a living? Then he spoke from his own experience: “I can assure you she has suffered plenty. ”The return has drawn heat. BetUS announced Russini on Nov. 9, and The Russini Report premiered two days later as a weekly show. She also writes a BetUS column and contributes to the podcast Nobody’s Safe, hosted by longtime friend Jon “Stugotz” Weiner. Guest Damon Amendolara said his mentions were a “horror show” after that first episode. TMZ’s sources say the debut drew so much traffic that it reportedly crashed on release day.
Article Summary: Sources close to the sports reporter say offers have poured in since Russini left The Athletic. The denial answers a claim Boston radio host Jim Murray made Friday. Murray said a friend of his spoke with Russini at Teddy Atlas’s annual dinner.

Article Title: India, Malaysia begin Harimau Shakti military drill with focus on counter-terror ops
Article Text:
Indian Army contingent in Malaysia for Exercise Hiramau Shakti. (Image credit: Indian Army)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The sixth edition of the India-Malaysia joint military exercise Harimau Shakti began on Friday at Ipoh in Malaysia, with 120 personnel from each side taking part. The exercise, a bilateral training event held alternately in the two countries, will run till November 30.The stated aim is to rehearse sub-conventional operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate, with particular emphasis on synergising responses during counter-terrorism missions. The two armies will work in jungle and semi-urban terrain, relying on joint planning, tactical coordination and emerging technologies to improve interoperability.The exercise will unfold in phases. In the first phase, troops will first undergo cross-training to familiarise themselves with each other's operating procedures, followed by joint tactical drills. These include setting up a Joint Command Post and Surveillance Centre, counter-terrorism operations, raids, cordon-and-search drills and combat engineering tasks. Special attention will go to Unmanned Aerial Systems for reconnaissance and surveillance, along with counter-drone capabilities to detect and neutralise hostile unmanned platforms. The exercise will end with a validation drill built around a simulated counter-terrorism scenario, combining ground operations, integrated surveillance and unmanned systems.The fifth edition was held last year at the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan from December 5 to 18 last year. The Indian contingent then largely comprised troops from the Dogra Regiment, while Malaysia was represented by the 25th Battalion of the Royal Malaysian Army.The exercise reflects a wider deepening of defence ties. India and Malaysia established diplomatic relations in 1957 and a Memorandum of Understanding on Defence Cooperation signed in 1993 gave military engagement an institutional framework. The Joint Defence Cooperation Committee reviews existing cooperation and identifies new areas. In August 2024, the two countries elevated their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.The naval dimension has grown as well. The fourth edition of Samudra Laksamana was held at Lumut from September 9 to 12 this year, with INS Mysore exercising alongside the Royal Malaysian Navy's KD Lekir and KD Gagah Samudera.In October 2025 INS Sahyadri visited Kemaman, while the survey vessel INS Sandhayak made a port call at Klang in July 2025. The navies of both nations also take part in multilateral platforms such as MILAN and the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise.Defence manufacturing is emerging as another area of cooperation. India is looking to expand exports to Southeast Asia, while Malaysia seeks to modernise its forces and diversify its sources of procurement. Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, Bharat Dynamics Limited and BEML showcased their products at LIMA 2025. The two countries are also co-chairing the SEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM) counter-terrorism working group for 2024-2027.
Article Summary: The sixth edition of the India-Malaysia joint military exercise Harimau Shakti began on Friday at Ipoh in Malaysia. The exercise, a bilateral training event held alternately in the two countries, will run till November 30. The stated aim is to rehearse sub-conventional operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate.

Article Title: 'Address: Tihar Jail, work: To Kill': How D-Company-linked gangster Naseem Durrani's long run ended in UP
Article Text:
Image Credit: TOI/ Special arrangement

How the net closed in

A chequered history





NEW DELHI: For years, Naseem Durrani moved between the gritty turf wars of northeast Delhi and the far-reaching shadow of Mumbai’s underworld — a man whose criminal ledger stretched from neighborhood extortion rackets to alleged hit contracts tied to Dawood Ibrahim ’s "D-Company."Beyond his crimes on the ground, Naseem actively used social media to cultivate a climate of fear among people. His Instagram profile served as an overt display of intimidation, featuring a bio that read: "Name: Badnaam (Notorious) | Address: Tihar Jail | Age: To live | Work: To kill." Through this digital persona, he openly advertised his criminal background while remaining absconding from law enforcement.On Friday, that long run ended in a hail of gunfire in Uttar Pradesh’s Bulandshahr district, where a joint operation by the Noida Special Task Force (STF) and Delhi Police cornered and killed the wanted gangster.Acting on intelligence inputs tracking Durrani’s movements, Delhi crime branch team led by DCP Sanjeev Yadav and deputy superintendent of police R K Mishra from STF Noida mounted a coordinated operation in Bulandshahr, supervised by special CP HGS Dhaliwal.In the early hours, the cops detected his movement near the Sikandra Bypass. CCTV footage showed him riding a scooter, and when the police team moved in to arrest him, he repeatedly looked back at the pursuing officers while speeding away.​During the chase, Naseem's scooter skidded and fell. Armed with two .32-bore pistols, he opened fire on the police team, prompting officers to retaliate. He sustained multiple gunshot wounds in the exchange of fire, and police recovered both pistols from the spot.The breakthrough came days after a brazen daylight-style shooting in northeast Delhi put law enforcement on high alert. Investigators had been scanning CCTV footage, tracing escape routes, and following leads in the wake of a deadly attack in Khajuri Khas.While police files linked Durrani to more than 25 criminal cases — spanning murder, attempt to murder, and robbery — his profile extended well beyond local street crime. The first was a killing outside Delhi law minister Kapil Mishra's camp office where 26-year-old Sameer was shot dead with over a dozen rounds fired in the attack.Police scrutiny following the recent violence has pointed to a prolonged gang feud in northeast Delhi, allegedly driven by extortion demands targeting shared auto-rickshaw operators and scrap dealers. Durrani had also previously been named as a key accused in the May 26 killing of Raja Mewati, alias "Akki Don," in Khajuri Khas.Investigators noted that Durrani had links to Dawood Ibrahim’s D-Company and remained in contact with underworld figure Chhota Shakeel. According to reports, Shakeel had allegedly handed Durrani a contract during 2016–2017 to eliminate rival gangster Chhota Rajan, who was lodged in Tihar Jail.With Durrani killed in the Bulandshahr encounter, investigators are expected to examine how his network operated across the Delhi-NCR and western Uttar Pradesh belt, as well as any lingering fallout from the ongoing turf wars in northeast Delhi.
Article Summary: Gangster Naseem Durrani was shot dead by police in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh. He was wanted in more than 25 criminal cases spanning murder, attempt to murder, and robbery. His criminal ledger stretched from neighborhood extortion rackets to alleged hit contracts tied to Dawood Ibrahim’s "D-Company"

In 2016, many public figures defended humans and humanity in the age of AI. Bill Gates made the case for “human reserved jobs”, such as caregivers, that should never be taken by machines, in a widely read essay.

Throughout history, the adjective human has signified people, as opposed to animals and gods (and, more recently, machines). Article Title: As Anthropic makes its Wall Street debut, CEO Dario Amodei says ‘We will not bend to either business or political pressure’
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

Here’s what CEO Dario Amodei said on Anthropic IPO

"My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas.

In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago.

I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety.

And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same.

We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission."

Claude-maker Anthropic made its blockbuster debut on Wall Street with the company’s valuation reaching nearly $2 trillion. Shares of the company closed at $97.17, up by 17% from its IPO price of $83. Soon after the debut, Anthropic shared a statement from CEO Dario Amodei reaffirming the company’s core focus on safety, committing to pace AI training and deployment as needed to maintain human control while resisting business or political pressures, framing this as essential to avoid risks like misuse or loss of control. “Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” Amodei said.“If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top,” he added.

Article Title: GTA 6 locations based on real places: 10 Florida landmarks and neighbourhoods recreated with fictional names in Leonida
Article Text:
PC: Rockstar Games

GTA 6 locations: From Miami's South Beach to the Everglades

Miami's South Beach becomes Ocean Beach

Little Havana as Little Cuba

Miami-Dade County inspires Vice-Dale County

Kaseya Center appears as Sahara Arena

Apalachicola National Forest as Mount Kalaga National Park

Miami International Airport gets a Vice City counterpart

PortMiami is recreated as Port Vice City

Florida Keys inspire the Leonida Keys

The Everglades become Grassrivers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Miami's Wynwood art as Stockyard

Grand Theft Auto 6 takes players to Leonida, a fictional US state inspired by Florida, where familiar real-world locations have been recreated with new names and identities. From Miami's South Beach, reimagined as Ocean Beach, to the Everglades-inspired Grassrivers and the island landscapes of the Leonida Keys, the game draws heavily on Florida's geography, architecture and natural environments. Other recognisable references include Little Havana, Miami International Airport, PortMiami and the Apalachicola National Forest. Here are 10 real places in Florida that have inspired GTA 6 locations.The stretch of coastline known for its Art Deco buildings, busy pavements and beachside activity has a counterpart in GTA 6 called Ocean Beach. It takes inspiration from South Beach and Ocean Drive in Miami, a connection confirmed on Rockstar's official website.Ocean Drive is one of the most recognisable parts of Miami's waterfront. Its architecture, hotels and restaurants have made the area a familiar feature of the city. In Leonida, Rockstar retains the coastal identity while giving the location a fictional name.Miami's Little Havana has been reimagined as Little Cuba in the game. Rockstar has confirmed the connection through its official website, making it one of the more clearly established geographical references in Leonida.The real neighbourhood is closely associated with Cuban-American culture. Calle Ocho, its best-known street, brings together restaurants, bakeries, cigar shops, art galleries and small businesses that have served the community for generations. Coffee windows known as ventanitas are also a familiar part of the area's street life.Little Havana has received recognition from the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which designated it a National Treasure. Its importance goes beyond tourism, with the neighbourhood serving as a centre of Cuban-American cultural life in Miami.Rockstar has also borrowed from Florida's administrative geography. Miami-Dade County, which includes Miami and several surrounding communities, has a fictional equivalent in GTA 6 called Vice-Dale County.The name follows a familiar approach used throughout the Grand Theft Auto series. Rather than reproduce the real location exactly, the developer changes parts of its name while keeping enough of the original reference recognisable.Here, Miami becomes Vice, a reference to Vice City, while Dade is changed to Dale.The Miami Heat's home venue has a counterpart in GTA 6 named Sahara Arena. The connection is based on footage from the game's first trailer, which offered viewers a look at a building resembling the Kaseya Center.Located in downtown Miami, the Kaseya Center is a major sports and entertainment venue. It hosts Miami Heat basketball games as well as concerts and other large events.Unlike Ocean Beach and Little Cuba, this particular reference is drawn from trailer footage rather than a direct listing on Rockstar's official website.Located near Leonida's northern border, Mount Kalaga National Park brings a different kind of landscape to GTA 6. Rather than the beaches and busy streets associated with Vice City, this part of the fictional state takes inspiration from the wooded wilderness of North Florida, particularly the Apalachicola National Forest.The real forest covers approximately 567,742 acres and is known for its longleaf pine woodlands, sandy trails, wetlands and winding waterways. Its landscape includes remote dirt roads and rivers darkened by tannins from surrounding vegetation. Florida has no substantial mountain ranges, making its northern forests a more fitting reference for Rockstar's rugged backcountry setting.Air travel also has a familiar presence in Leonida. Miami International Airport, one of Florida's busiest aviation hubs, is represented by Vice City International Airport.The connection comes from Rockstar's trailer footage, which includes scenes showing an airport resembling its real-world counterpart. The naming follows the same pattern used for several other locations, replacing Miami with Vice City.Miami International Airport is a major gateway for domestic and international travellers, particularly those travelling between the United States, Latin America and the Caribbean. Its position in South Florida makes it a natural reference for a game drawing so heavily on the region.The waterfront infrastructure of Miami has also influenced the game's setting. PortMiami appears to have inspired Port Vice City, a location shown in the trailers.The real port occupies Dodge Island in Biscayne Bay, close to Fisher Island and Star Island. It is an important part of Miami's maritime landscape, with cruise terminals and cargo facilities forming a large part of its operations.Its island setting is one of the geographical details that makes the comparison interesting. The port is not simply another building in the city's skyline but an extensive waterfront area with a distinct position within Miami's coastal geography.South of mainland Florida, the chain of islands known as the Florida Keys provides another reference for GTA 6. Rockstar's official website identifies the Leonida Keys as the game's version of the real archipelago.Florida is replaced with Leonida, while the word Keys remains unchanged. The actual Florida Keys are known for their island communities, coastal roads and access to the surrounding waters. The region also includes natural areas such as Bahia Honda State Park and Dagny Johnson Key Largo Hammock Botanical State Park.One of Florida's most distinctive natural environments has been given a different identity in GTA 6. The Everglades appear in the game as Grassrivers, a region of Leonida that Rockstar describes on its official website as a major natural feature of the fictional state.The real Everglades is a vast wetland system in southern Florida. Often described as a slow-moving river of grass, its shallow freshwater flows south from Lake Okeechobee towards the Gulf of Mexico.Its landscape is far from uniform. Sawgrass marshes cover extensive areas, while cypress forests, mangroves and elevated hardwood habitats known as hammocks form other parts of the ecosystem. The ground beneath much of the region consists of limestone and marl, generally covered by layers of organic material and some sand.Stockyard is one of the locations featured in Rockstar Games' upcoming title Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), set in the fictional state of Leonida. As players explore Vice City and its surrounding areas, Stockyard adds another layer to the game's detailed urban landscape. Its name and appearance have prompted interest among fans trying to identify possible real-world connections and understand which parts of Florida may have influenced its design.
Article Summary: GTA 6 takes players to Leonida, a fictional US state inspired by Florida. familiar real-world locations have been recreated with new names and identities. Other recognisable references include Little Havana, Miami International Airport, PortMiami and the Apalachicola National Forest.

Article Title: Microsoft staff wrote open letter that they fear being replaced by AI, then 60,000 got exit offers; Satya Nadella now says: Why do we need software engineers? To...
Article Text:
​What Nadella sees next for every Microsoft job​​

Nadella says every job at Microsoft will turn into managing AI agents

Microsoft employees had already put their AI worries in writing

Microsoft’s 60,000 buyout offer covers teams in India, US, Canada and UK

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has given his clearest explanation yet for why the company asked around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its workforce, to consider leaving. Speaking to Andrew Ross Sorkin at the NYT DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Nadella said the buyout was meant “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices” as Microsoft rebuilds itself around AI. His comments come weeks after a group of Microsoft workers circulated an open letter. It accused the company of chasing AI with a “speed-at-all-costs” ethos and flagged “threats of AI job replacement and layoffs.”Nadella made it clear that the plan is not to swap engineers for AI.“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he said.Some people, he admitted, find “that reorganization and change is sort of hard,” but “it has to be done.”To show what that new operating point looks like, Nadella pointed to the team behind Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. The team has just 11 developers, and they have learnt to let AI do most of the building. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product,” he said.He expects every employee to eventually direct AI agents instead of doing the work themselves.“That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs,” Nadella said. He also admitted that a 51-year-old company was not born AI-first, and that the shift “is going to take a bit more time than anyone expects.”On a podcast with Gergely Orosz last week, he went a step further. He said the industry had “created enormous anxiety” among workers with talk of the singularity and of AI taking away all jobs.Before the buyouts were announced, current and former employees circulated a letter signed “Concerned Microsoft Workers.” It called working at the company “joyless and demoralizing.” According to the letter, staff were pushed to use AI in almost every area with little training, and were spending time “fixing AI slop” and reworking low-quality features.The letter asked Microsoft to involve workers in decisions on AI and to stop tying AI use to rewards, reprimands or layoffs. It also asked the company to treat AI as an assistive tool rather than “a complete labor replacement.”Six employees told the NYT that the buyout landed on a workforce already strained by AI targets and stagnant pay, with some merit raises this year below 1%. Gretchen Thomas, a design leader who left in September, had her stock award cut. According to a memo seen by the NYT, part of the reason was that she did “not consistently” show speed, urgency and willingness to experiment, including with AI.Microsoft confirmed the Voluntary Exit Offer on October 26. It covers employees at vice president level and below on select teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK. Xbox, Windows, Copilot and Finance are among the divisions involved.Employees have until December 9 to decide, and those who accept will leave on December 31 with at least eight weeks of base pay. Microsoft expects fewer than 5% to take it. This is its second buyout this year, after a retirement-age offer earlier in 2026. It also follows layoffs of 10,000 people in 2023, over 15,000 in 2025 and about 4,800 this summer.Chief people officer Amy Coleman told the NYT that the buyouts were not linked to how AI is changing work, and she did not rule out future layoffs. Two days after the offer, Microsoft reported quarterly profit of $36.6 billion, up 32%. Capital spending, mostly on data centres, rose 30% to $45.2 billion, and the company expects to spend roughly $170 billion this year.For those who stay, the worry is more immediate. Employees told the NYT they do not expect departing colleagues to be replaced, so their work will land on the people left behind. That is where Nadella’s new operating point will be tested first.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says every job at the company will turn into managing AI agents. He made it clear that the plan is not to swap engineers for AI. Microsoft confirmed the Voluntary Exit Offer on October 26. It covers employees at vice president level and below on select teams in US, Canada, India and UK.
